name: Bitpaidio staking top-up keeps the matured lock time
summary: Bitpaidio Staking.Lock_Token added a new amount to an existing lock while keeping its original start and end time, and withdraw paid the whole locked amount plus a fixed 5% ROI once end_time had passed. The attacker opened empty plan-1 locks from a batch of contracts, waited six months, then from each contract flash-borrowed BTP from the BTP/USDT pair, topped up the matured lock and withdrew it with 5% ROI in the same transaction, compounding the profit over 23 transactions.
notes: Re-anchored from the reported 0x1ae499cc (block 28176676), the attacker's 23rd and last successful flash-withdraw; 0x1f0f3aef is the first. The attacker created the lock-holding contracts and opened their zero-amount locks in 0xd4ee8a5a six months earlier, which took nothing; its later flash attempts reverted. No other account ever withdrew more than it locked plus the 5% ROI.

The BTP/USDT pair held 112,110 BTP and 45,597 USDT before the campaign, so the 226,806 BTP taken (DefiLlama $89k) could not be absorbed; it is valued at the 30,028.20 USDT the attacker's two sales realised (rule 12).
Non-upgradeable with the token fixed in the constructor and ROI rates without setters, so the deployment sets the age.
